documents.title: Doc 47 - DECISION - Car 18 - Right of Review
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 18 - Right of Review

details.fact: Car 18 (Badoer) made nose to tail contact with Car 3 (Rivera) at turn 14 after Car 3 experienced an electrical problem and loss of power.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: In relation to the penalty applied to Car 18 in Document 30 we determine: a. The penalty is rescinded. b. The 10 seconds added to the elapsed race time of Car 18 on the provisional results shall be removed when preparing and issuing the final classification. c. The two (2) penalty points added to the driver’s record shall be removed. Total for the 2026 season = 0 points. d. No Further Action is taken in relation to the collision between Car 18 and Car 3 at Turn 14.
details.reason: During the Sprint Race, the Stewards issued an in-race 10 seconds penalty to Car 18 (BAD) for causing a collision with Car 3 (RIV). This penalty was issued during the session without a hearing based on the video evidence available. After the Sprint Race, the Team Manager of RIV informed the Stewards that RIV suffered an electrical failure on the exit of Turn 14 which caused it to lose power. The Stewards, having determined that this information constituted a significant, new and relevant element that was unavailable to them at the time of the decision, decided to re- examine Decision Document N. 30, pursuant Article 14.1.2 of the FIA International Sporting Code. The team representatives were summoned and heard. The Team Manager of RIV confirmed the technical failure which caused the loss of power of RIV at Turn 14 while BAD was approaching at full speed. The Team Manager of BAD stated that the driver had no time to react and to avoid RIV in front of him, who was losing power and speed. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that BAD was merely trying to avoid a stricken car, that he tried his best to avoid RIV, and that neither driver is wholly or predominantly responsible for the collision. Accordingly, the findings and penalties set forth in Document 30 are hereby vacated and revised as set forth herein.

documents.title: DOC 54 -2026 Budapest Event - DECISION - Car 5 - Allegedly causing a collision with Car 8
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 5 - Allegedly causing a collision with Car 8

details.fact: On Lap 1, Car 5 (Slater) collided with the rear of Car 8 (Taponen) on the approach to Turn 12.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the 2026 FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video evidence. Car 8 (Taponen) was ahead of Car 5 (Slater) through Turn 11. Car 5 achieved a better exit and carried greater momentum towards Turn 12.. After exiting the corner, Car 8 moved progressively towards the right-hand side of the track, reducing the available gap. At the same time, Car 5 attempted to enter that narrowing gap. The available video evidence did not establish whether Car 8 was reacting to the movement of Car 5 or whether Car 5 had committed to the gap before Car 8 began closing it. The cars’ converging trajectories resulted in contact between the left side of the front wing of Car 5 and the right-rear wheel of Car 8. Car 8 sustained a puncture and entered the Pit Lane. The consequence of the contact does not, by itself, determine responsibility. Based on the available evidence, the Stewards could not establish that either driver was wholly or predominantly responsible for the collision and therefore decide to take no further action.

documents.title: DOC 53 -2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 1 - Forcing car 8 off track at Turn 1 in Lap 24
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 1 - Forcing car 8 off track at Turn 1 in Lap 24

details.fact: At Turn 1 on Lap 24, Car 8 (Taponen) was forced off the track while attempting to overtake Car 1 (Nael).
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(b) of the International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A ten-second time penalty, imposed in accordance with Article 39.3(b) of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, two penalty points are added to the driver’s record. The driver’s total for the 2026 season is 5 penalty points.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video evidence and summoned and heard from the drivers of Car 1 (Nael) and Car 8 (Taponen), together with their team representatives (Documents 43 and 44). On the approach to Turn 1 on Lap 24, Car 1 was on the right (on the inside of the corner), while Car 8 was positioned on the left and attempted to overtake around the outside. The video evidence showed that the front axle of Car 8 was ahead of the front axle of Car 1 at the apex. Car 1 subsequently failed to leave Car 8 sufficient racing room at the exit, resulting in Car 8 being forced off the track. The driver of Car 1 stated that he considered Car 8 was not ahead at the apex and had therefore not earned the right to racing room at the exit. The driver of Car 8 expressed the opposite view. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 8 had satisfied the requirements of the FIA Formula 3 Driving Standards Guidelines for an overtaking car on the outside and was therefore entitled to racing room at the exit of Turn 1. Car 1 failed to provide that room and forced Car 8 off the track. The Stewards therefore impose the baseline ten-second time penalty in line with previous precedents,

documents.title: DOC 52 -2026 Budapest Event - DECISION - Car 1 - Allegedly forcing Car 8 off track at Turn 2 in Lap 21
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 1 - Allegedly forcing Car 8 off track at Turn 2 in Lap 21

details.fact: Car 1 (Nael) allegedly forced Car 8 (Taponen) off the track at Turn 2 on Lap 21.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (b) of the 2026 FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video evidence and summoned and heard from the drivers of Car 1 (Nael) and Car 8 (Taponen), together with their team representatives (Documents 43 and 44). On the approach to Turn 2 on Lap 21, Car 1 was positioned on the left (on the inside of the corner) while Car 8 was on the right and attempted to overtake Car 1 around the outside of Turn 2. The FIA Formula 3 Driving Standards Guidelines provide that, to be entitled to racing room at the exit when overtaking on the outside, the overtaking car must have its front axle ahead of the front axle of the other car at the apex. Based on the available video angles and the differing accounts provided by the drivers, the Stewards could not determine conclusively whether Car 8 had achieved the required overlap relative to Car 1 at the apex and earning him entitlement to racing room at the exit. Furthermore, as the cars exited Turn 2, Car 8 ran wide but maintained two wheels in contact with the track. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the matter was marginal and were not satisfied that the available evidence established that Car 1 had breached the regulations. The Stewards therefore decide to take no further action.

The driver of Car 1 stated that he considered Car 8 was not ahead at the apex and had therefore not earned the right to racing room at the exit. The driver of Car 8 expressed the opposite view. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 8 had satisfied the requirements of the FIA Formula 3 Driving Standards Guidelines for an overtaking car on the outside and was therefore entitled to racing room at the exit of Turn 1. Car 1 failed to provide that room and forced Car 8 off the track. As mitigating circumstances, the Stewards considered that the incident occurred immediately following a Safety Car restart and that the presence of Car 7 directly ahead restricted the available space and affected the approach of Car 1 to the corner. The Stewards therefore impose a five-second time penalty.

documents.title: DOC 49 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 29 - Erratic driving
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 29 - Erratic driving

details.fact: Car 29 (Lacorte) made more than one change of direction while defending against Car 9 (Giusti) between Turns 5 and 6.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(b) of the International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A ten-second time penalty, imposed in accordance with Article 39.3(b) of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, two (2) penalty points are added to the driver’s record. The driver’s total for the 2026 season is 2 penalty points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. On Lap 16, after exiting Turn 5 and while approaching Turn 6, Car 29 (Lacorte) made two changes of direction while defending against Car 9 (Giusti). Car 29 initially moved to the right, away from the racing line, before subsequently moving back to the left towards the racing line as the cars approached the braking zone for Turn 6. When returning towards the racing line, Car 29 did not leave at least one car width between his car and the edge of the track. This movement caused Car 9 to take evasive action, lose traction under braking, and leave the track at Turn 6. Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(b) of the International Sporting Code provides that more than one change of direction to defend a position is not permitted. It further provides that a driver returning towards the racing line after defending off-line must leave at least one car width between their car and the edge of the track on the approach to a corner. Having considered the incident in its entirety, the Stewards determined that Car 29 made more than one change of direction while defending and was wholly responsible for causing Car 9 to leave the track. The Stewards therefore impose a ten-second time penalty. In addition, two penalty points are added to the driver’s record in accordance with the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Penalty Guidelines.

documents.title: DOC 46 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Race 2 - Safety Car infringement - multiple cars
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Race 2 - Safety Car infringement - multiple cars

details.fact: The Cars below entered Pit Lane during the Safety Car deployment that occurred at 08:46.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 40.11 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations
details.decision: Reprimand (driving) for all cars listed above.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video, timing data, and GPS data. The evidence showed that the cars listed above entered the Pit Lane while the Safety Car was deployed. The Race Director had not instructed the cars to use the Pit Lane, and the marshalling light panels clearly indicated that the cars were to remain on the track. Article 40.11 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations states: “Other than when the cars and the safety car are required to use the pit lane, no car may enter the pits whilst the safety car is deployed unless it is for the purpose of changing damaged tyres, or a change of climatic conditions necessitates the use of a different specification of tyre or repairing a genuine accident damage.” None of the exceptions permitted under Article 40.11 applied. The Stewards therefore determine that each driver breached Article 40.11 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. Ordinarily, such a breach, particularly if committed by one car or a limited number of cars, would warrant a more significant sporting penalty. However, the Stewards note that all the cars concerned entered the Pit Lane and that none stopped at their designated garage area, conducted a pit stop, or derived a sporting advantage. The Stewards consider these circumstances sufficiently mitigating to impose a Reprimand. This decision arises from the exceptional circumstances of this incident, which involved a collective failure by the drivers concerned. It should not be regarded as establishing a precedent. Any similar breach in the future will be assessed independently, having regard to its particular facts, circumstances, and sporting consequences.

documents.title: DOC 35 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 25 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 25 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 25 (Nakamura) collided with Car 31 (Xie) on Lap 1 and on the approach to Turn 2.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty, which since Car 25 was not classified, is converted to a drop of 3 places on the grid for the next Feature Race in which the driver participates. In addition, 1 point to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers of Car 25 (Nakamura) and Car 31 (Xie), together with their Team Representatives (Documents 27 and 28). Video evidence showed that, on the approach to Turn 2 on Lap 1, Car 25 was behind Car 31. As the field compressed into the corner, Car 31 moved to the left in response to the cars ahead and to avoid contact. Car 25 continued to close on Car 31 but was unable to avoid colliding with the rear of Car 31. The Driver of Car 25 stated that he had not anticipated the rate at which he was closing on Car 31. He further stated that Car 31 moved suddenly to the left immediately before the collision, leaving insufficient time to react and avoid contact. The Driver of Car 31 stated that he moved to the left to avoid the cars ahead, which were slowing into Turn 2, and that the collision occurred while carrying out that manoeuvre. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 25 was predominantly at fault for the collision, having failed to react to his closing speed in relation to Car 31 and causing the collision. While Car 31 moved to the left to avoid the cars ahead, this did not relieve Car 25 of its responsibility to avoid the collision. As the incident occurred on the opening lap, the Stewards took this into account as a mitigating factor and imposed a five (5) second time penalty in accordance with the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Penalty Guidelines. Since Car 25 was not classified, the penalty is converted to a three (3) place grid drop for the next Feature Race in which the driver participates, in accordance with the Article 39.3(d) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations.

documents.title: DOC 20 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Parc ferme violation
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Parc ferme violation

details.fact: Mechanics of Car 14 (Yamakoshi) worked on the car after the end-of-race signal had been issued.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 44.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. Breach of Article 2.5.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: - Car 14 is disqualified from the Qualifying session. - All lap times set during the session are deleted. - Car 14 is granted permission to start both the Sprint and Feature races from the back of the grid.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Driver of Car 14 (Yamakoshi) and the Team Representative (Document 17). Video footage showed that, prior to the end-of-race signal being given, Car 14 was in its pit stop position and was being worked on. After the end-of-race signal was given, mechanics continued to work on the car for approximately a further two minutes. The Team Representative confirmed the facts and explained that Car 14 had experienced engine issues during the session and that the Driver entered the pit lane for repairs. He further explained that the team required assistance from the engine supplier to carry out the repairs; however, the repairs could not be completed before the end of the session. The Team Representative stated that the team then needed to ensure that the car could return to parc fermé under its own power and without assistance. The Stewards accept the Team's explanation and acknowledge that the Team was not seeking to gain any sporting advantage and was, in fact, attempting to avoid causing any unnecessary delay to the end-of-session procedures. Nonetheless, working on a car after the end-of-race signal has been given is prohibited by the Sporting Regulations, as parc fermé conditions commence upon the issuance of the end-of-race signal. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards find that a breach of the regulations has occurred and accordingly impose the standard penalty of disqualification for a breach of parc fermé conditions.

documents.title: Doc 80 - DECISION - Car 22 - Alleged contact with Car 4
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 22 - Alleged contact with Car 4

details.fact: Car 4 (Stromsted) and Car 22 (Garfias) collided at Turn 2.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (documents 73 and 74). Car 22 (GAR) was attempting an inside pass of Car 4 (STR) at T1 and had properly established his rights to the corner since he was slightly ahead at the apex. GAR did not make a full exit at Turn 1 which leads directly into the second part of the chicane. This allowed STR to remain on track and maintain partial overlap with GAR approaching Turn 2. STR ran out of room at the apex of Turn 2 where the cars collided causing GAR to spin. Generally, in chicanes, the car that established its rights in the first corner has the rights to the entire segment; however, it remains possible for the car that lost the rights to the first corner to reestablish its rights in the second corner. Once GAR allowed STR to remain on track after Turn 1, STR was entitled to fight back at Turn 2, and he did. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that even though GAR had the initial rights to the chicane, under the circumstances, STR had the right to contest Turn 2. Even though GAR remained ahead on the outside of Turn 2, he could not reasonably expect STR to disappear and he could have allowed STR more racing room on the inside of Turn 2. Having lost the rights at T1, STR could have declined to push the position, and GAR, having allowed STR to remain on track, could have allowed him more room at Turn 2. The Stewards determine that neither driver is wholly or predominantly at fault for the collision. Given that both drivers could have taken steps to avoid the collision, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

details.fact: During the reconnaissance laps Car 23 (Shin) was released from its pit position into the path of Car 14 (Yamakoshi).

details.decision: Warning to the Team
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (documents 44 and 45). Car 23 (SHI) was released from its pit position into path of Car 14 (YAM). The Stewards determine that a practice start infringement occurred, but in light of the forgoing mitigating circumstances elect to issue a warning which is less than the standard penalty for such an infraction.

documents.title: Doc 28 - INFRIGEMENT - Car 20 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRIGEMENT - Car 20 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 20 (Sharp) collided with Car 21 (Wharton) at Turn 5.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten second (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 points.
details.reason: The stewards examined video and telemetry evidence. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine Cars 20 (SHA) and 21 (WHA) had been racing hard since Turn 1 with WHA leading. They got side by side in Turn 3 and SHA attempted an outside pass on (WHA) at Turn 4. SHA was not ahead at the apex and had not earned the right to be given room on the exit. WHA properly made a full exit which caused SHA to exceed track limits on the exit. The stewards accept that SHA could not simply disappear even though he was obliged to concede the corner. At this point, SHA was required to rejoin safely and without gaining a lasting advantage. Telemetry indicated that SHA maintained full throttle in the runoff area which put him in position to set up for an inside pass at Turn 5. Being in position to attack, when he should have properly conceded, constituted an advantage to which SHA was not entitled. WHA turned into Turn 5 and collided with SHA who was midway alongside. Regardless of the question of gaining an advantage, SHA had not established sufficient position to have gained the right to racing room on the inside. The stewards determine that SHA is wholly responsible for the collision and elect to apply the standard penalty.

details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 11 (GLA) was attempting an inside overtake on Car 11 (TAP) at turn 18. TAP turned in earlier than normal as part of his defense thus squeezing GLA while still leaving him racing room. GLA did not have his front axle alongside TAP’s mirror prior to the apex which means that he had not won the corner. While this would ordinarily mean that he was responsible for any ensuing collision, the stewards determine that TAP’s defensive move was made late enough that he contributed to the collision. Under the circumstances, the Stewards do not find either driver to be wholly or predominantly responsible for the collision. Based on the totality of the circumstances, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 63 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Technical infringement

details.fact: The front push rod LH - CPL (part number: F32506D001) of car #14 was mounted on the right-hand side of the car and the front push rod RH - CPL (part number: F32506D002) was mounted on the left-hand side of the car.
details.infringement: Breach of Articles 1.5.3 and 17.1 of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Car 14 is disqualified from the Sprint Race classification. All other drivers move up in the classification.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 61) and the FIA Formula 3 Technical Delegate. During the hearing the team representative acknowledged that the facts as stated above are true and correct: specifically, that the front push rod LH - CPL (part number: F32506D001) of car #14 was mounted on the right-hand side of the car and the front push rod RH - CPL (part number: F32506D002) was mounted on the left- hand side of the car. The team representative disputed that these facts constitute a breach of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations. (For the sake of convenience any and all Article references hereinafter contained are with respect to the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.) While the Technical Delegate’s report included a reference to Article 1.5.2, it is not alleged that the parts in question were modified. They were not. The question at hand is whether the parts were installed on the wrong side of the car. The FIA Technical Delegate and the team representative both referred to the language of Article Article 1.5.3 and Article 17.1 The relevant part of Article 1.5.3 provides, “For the avoidance of doubt the original design and construction of the car must be maintained at all times.” Article 17.1 titled General Principles begins, “The complete car is divided into three types of parts. The parts are classified in the spare parts catalogue.” The stewards find that the “original design and construction of the car” is illuminated by Article 17.1. It is clear that the car is made up of parts and that the parts are specified in the spare parts catalogue. The front pushrod is depicted on page 006D of the spare parts catalogue which also includes line references to “front push rod LH – CPL” (part number: F32506D001) and “front push rod RH – CPL” (part number: F32506D002) are listed on page 006G of the catalogue. The Technical Delegate explained that the front push rod LH is meant to be installed on the left hand side of the car, and vice versa. The team’s contention is that “LH” and “RH” are not defined within the spare parts catalogue as “left side” and “right side” and that, in the absence of a formal definition, the matter is unclear, vague and easily subject to misinterpretation. Given the alleged ambiguity, they feel that the car is compliant notwithstanding the facts of the installation. The stewards acknowledge that references to left or right with respect to a race car are taken to mean left or right from the driver’s point of view. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that the abbreviations LH and RH, which are used extensively throughout the catalogue, and are so commonplace within the world at large as to not reasonably require express definition within the sophisticated world of Formula 3. Furthermore, if the team had any confusion about what the abbreviations meant they had ample opportunity to seek clarification from the Technical Delegate and they did not do so. The stewards also note that the lower front wishbones (part number: F32506G001 and F32506G002) to which these parts connect are also designated and labeled as LH and RH. The Technical Delegate confirmed that the wishbones were correctly installed on the expected left hand and right hand sides of the car. In this case, the team connected front pushrod LH to front lower wishbone RH, and vice versa. The team points out that regardless of a parts name, many part's can only successfully be installed on one side of the car. While that may be true, the stewards believe that even in face of alleged ambiguity or confusion, the team ought to notice that the parts that wind up on the right hand side of the car are designated RH, and that the parts that wind up on the left hand side of the car are designated LH. Accordingly, the stewards further determine the meaning of LH and RH should be clear to the team based on its overall experience with the car and its numerous parts over time. The stewards determine that the front push rod LH – CPL must be installed on the left hand side of the car and that the front push rod RH – CPL must be installed on the right hand side of the car. The stewards determine that Articles 1.5.3 and 17.1 of FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations have therefore been breached and that the standard penalty of a disqualification needs to be applied for such an infringement.

documents.title: Doc 31 - DECISION - Car 8 - Alleged unsafe release
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 8 - Alleged unsafe release

details.fact: Car 8 (Taponen) was released nearly simultaneously with Car 4 (Stromsted) at the beginning of Qualifying Session A.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (Documents 22 & 23). It is undisputed that Car 4 (STR), who had just been released into the fast lane, had to brake to avoid Car 8 (TAP). Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that both cars were released nearly simultaneously with TAP moving before any wheel of STR’s car entered the fast lane. Unfortunately, there was a car in between the pair which hindered STR’s ability to notice that TAP was moving as well. This contributed to the cars being in close proximity before STR was able to react. The stewards further note that at the moment STR was being released, a television cameraman walked in between the crewmember releasing TAP and the front of TAP’s car, thus obscuring his vision of STR’s release and adding an element of distraction to the release process. Given the totality of these circumstances, the stewards do not find any fault with respect to the decision to release. To the extent that the situation was unsafe at all, it was predominantly attributable to the presence of the car between these two blocking the view on this tight pit lane and the actions of the cameraman. Accordingly, the stewards decide to take no further action.

documents.title: DOC 64 - 2026 Monza Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 28 - Unsafe re-join
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 28 - Unsafe re-join

details.fact: Car 28 (Barichello) re-joined the track unsafely Turn 1.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 c) of the FIA International Sporting Code
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. As the penalty could not be served in-race, it will be converted to a 3 place grid drop for his next Feature Race. In addition, 1 point to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 1 point.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (Documents 53 & 54). Having been forced off track by Car 18 (BAD), Car 28 (BAR) re-joined and had a collision with BAD. Once a car is off-track it is permitted to rejoin; however, this can only be done when it is safe to do so. The obligation to make a safe re-entry is the same whether the driver went off track on their own or if they were forced off. In this case, BAR collided with BAD immediately after re-joining. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that BAR made an unsafe re-entry. In many cases, a driver has a reasonably large amount of time to determine when, where, and how, they will re-enter. BAR’s window for making the decision to re-join was fairly compressed due to his proximity to Turn 1. On account of that mitigating circumstance, the Stewards elect to impose a reduced penalty for this infraction. The Stewards would like to acknowledge the collision itself for which they find neither driver to be wholly or predominantly at fault. BAR contributed to it by the unsafe re- rejoin for which he has been penalized herein, and BAD bears some fault for having forced BAR off, thus necessitating BAR’s rejoin (see Document 63 for BAD’s penalty). The Stewards believe that the interests of justice are best served by the two decisions dealing with the collective conduct that ultimately led to the collision.

documents.title: DOC 42 - 2026 Monza Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - Breach of Sporting Regulations Article 24.6
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - Breach of Sporting Regulations Article 24.6

details.fact: One set of dry-weather tyres allocated to Car 5 was not returned within the specified time.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 24.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of €2,500 is imposed on the Team. €2,000 of this amount is suspended for the remainder of the 2026 Formula 3 season in accordance with Article 12.4.6 of the FIA International Sporting Code, subject to there being no further breach by the Team of Article 24.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. The remaining €500 shall be paid in accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code. The fine must be paid within forty-eight hours of notification by bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards received a report from the FIA Technical Delegate. They summoned the Team Representative (document 41) and heard the Team Representative, two members of the Team’s Operational Personnel, and the FIA Technical Delegate. The Stewards determined that one set of dry-weather tyres allocated to Car 5 was not deposited in the FIA Formula 3 tyre Parc Fermé within the time specified by the FIA Technical Delegate. The tyres concerned remained fitted to Car 5 while the car was under Parc Fermé conditions. However, once the car was released from Parc Fermé, the tyres were outside the designated tyre Parc Fermé for a short period before being deposited there. Article 24.6 requires all allocated dry-weather tyres to be stored in the designated secure area during the times specified by the FIA Technical Delegate. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that, while the Competitor did not gain a sporting advantage, the Competitor was nevertheless in breach of Article 24.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. Taking into account the mitigating circumstances, the Stewards considered a fine to be the appropriate penalty, in line with previous precedent.

documents.title: DOC 39 - 2026 Monza Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Technical infringement

details.fact: The rear diffuser of Car 6 is lower than the minimum height stipulated in Article 3.4.1a.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 3.4.1a of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Disqualification of Car 6 from the Classification of Qualifying Group A. Removal of all times set by car 6 in the Qualifying Session. All cars originally classified behind Car 6 are moved up one place in the Group A Qualifying Classification. Pursuant to Article 34.2 of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations, permission is given for Car 6 to start the Sprint Race and the Feature Race from the back of the grid after any other penalties have been applied in accordance with Article 34.5 f.
details.reason: The Stewards received the Technical Report (document 35). They summoned the Driver and Team Representative (document 36). The Driver was invited but declined to attend. The Team Representative and the Technical Delegate attended the hearing. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the height of the diffusor of Car 6 was found to be below the required minimum height stipulated in Article 3.4.1.a of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations. Specifically, even after the tolerance defined in Article 3.4.2 is applied, the rear diffusor is 3mm below the limit on the left-hand side. The measurement was conducted by the Technical Delegate using the standard method. The measurement was taken on multiple occasions for verification, and the FIA platform was also confirmed to be in correct set up. The Team Representative stated, and the Stewards acknowledge, that following the accident that occurred during the Free Practice session, the Team was unable to inspect the car on the official platform as the repairs took a considerable amount of time. Nevertheless, the Stewards determine that it is responsibility of the Competitor to ensure the compliance of the car with the Technical Regulations throughout the Competition. The Stewards therefore issue the disqualification as the standard penalty for a technical infringement.

details.fact: Car 2 (UGO) collided with Car 6 (DEP) on the front straight.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Drop of five grid positions for the Sprint and Feature Races at this Event in accordance with Article 39.3 (g) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 penalty points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives of Car 2 and Car 6 (documents 15 and 16). Car 6 (DEP) attempted to pass Car 2 (UGO) on the front straight with both cars already to the right of center of the track. UGO immediately moved right to defend, and continued moving toward the track edge. UGO’s defence crowded DEP beyond the edge of the track, at which point a collision occurred between DEP’s left front wing and UGO’s right rear tyre causing a puncture. UGO’s car also left the track before a secondary collision which resulted in DEP hitting the wall. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that DEP made a legitimate pass attempt and that UGO’s attempted defensive move was too late. Furthermore, UGO was not entitled to crowd DEP beyond the edge of the track and therefore the Stewards conclude that UGO was wholly responsible for the collision. In determining the penalty, which is greater than past precedents for collisions in Free Practice, the Stewards considered the lateness of the move, the unjustified crowding beyond track limits and the fact that such vigorous defense is unnecessary within the confines of Free Practice.

documents.title: Doc 75 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Technical infringement

details.fact: The rear diffuser of Car 6 was found to be lower than the minimum height stipulated in Article 3.4.1a of the 2026 FIA F3 Technical Regulations.
details.infringement: Article 3.4.1.a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Disqualification of Car 6 from the Classification of Race 2 (Feature). All cars originally classified behind Car 6 are moved up one place in the Race classification. All lap times set by Car 6 during the Race are cancelled.
details.reason: The Stewards, having received the report of the Technical Delegate (Document 57), summoned (Document 62) and heard the driver of Car 6 (De Palo), the Team Representative and the Race Engineer. The Technical Delegate reported that, following Race 2, the diffuser of Car 6 was found to be below the minimum height required by Article 3.4.1.a of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations. After the 5 mm tolerance under Article 3.4.2 had been taken into account, the diffuser measured up to 3 mm below the minimum on the right-hand side and 1 mm below the minimum on the left-hand side. The Team Representative confirmed the measurements taken by the Technical Delegate. The team submitted, however, that Car 6 had received a number of rear impacts from Car 5 (Slater), the Driver's team-mate, during Race 2, most likely in the diffuser area, and invited the Stewards to review the footage in support of that account. The Stewards reviewed the footage of the final two laps of Race 2 and confirmed that Car 5 made contact with Car 6 on two occasions during that period. The Stewards and the Technical Delegate inspected Car 5 and observed some damage to its front wing. On inspection of Car 6, the Stewards observed only very minimal scratches to the rear diffuser. The Race Engineer stated his belief that the contact from Car 5 may have caused a deformation or bending of the diffuser plates. Article 11.7.3 of the ISC provides that, where the regulations place the burden of proof on the person alleged to have committed a breach, that person must satisfy the Stewards, on the balance of probability, that the fact asserted is more likely than not to be true. Under Article 1.4 of the Technical Regulations, the car must comply with the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations in their entirety at all times during a Competition, and under Article 1.8 it is the duty of the Competitor to satisfy the Technical Delegate and the Stewards that its car so complies. The burden of establishing compliance therefore rests, at all times, with the Competitor. The longstanding jurisprudence of the FIA International Court of Appeal (the "ICA") holds that a breach of the technical regulations must lead to disqualification unless the Competitor has committed no fault, whether intentionally or through negligence, and the non-conformity is the result of exceptional circumstances. These two conditions are cumulative, and exceptional circumstances are admitted only under very limited criteria. The ICA has likewise declined to accept an in-race incident as the cause of a technical irregularity where the physical condition of the car does not support that account (ICA-2014-03). Applying that framework, the breach is established and is not disputed. The Team Representative confirmed the measurements, and the Stewards are comfortably satisfied that the diffuser of Car 6 was below the minimum height permitted by Article 3.4.1.a after the applicable tolerance. The burden then rests on the Competitor to show, on the balance of probability, that the car was compliant before the contact and that the contact from Car 5 caused the non-conformity. The Stewards considered whether the contact from Car 5 was, by itself, enough to relieve the Competitor of the consequence of the non-conformity. The Stewards accepted that contact occurred twice. The burden, however, was on the Competitor to show that it was more likely than not that the contact caused the non-conformity, and the Competitor produced nothing to meet it. Beyond the assertion that the contact may have deformed the diffuser, no evidence was put before the Stewards connecting the contact to the measurements found. The very minimal scratches observed on Car 6 showed no breakage consistent with a displacing impact. The Technical Delegate confirms that the diffuser assembly was properly fixed and they did not note any displacement or misalignment. With no evidence before them capable of tipping the balance of probability in the Competitor's favour, the Stewards cannot treat the contacts as the cause of the breach. The Competitor has therefore not met the burden upon it. In-race contact of this nature does not meet the strict and narrow criteria for exceptional circumstances recognized by the International Court of Appeal. For these reasons, and having considered the matters raised extensively, the Stewards find that Car 6 is in breach of Article 3.4.1.a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations, and that the Competitor has not provided evidence capable of relieving it of its obligation to ensure the conformity of the car. The Stewards therefore issue the disqualification as a standard penalty for a technical infringement.

documents.title: Doc 67 - DECISION - Car 21 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 21 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage

details.fact: Car 21 (Wharton) left the track at Turn 6 and gained a lasting advantage over Car 27 (David)
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations Alleged Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (c) of the FIA International Sporting Code
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined the video evidence, summoned (Documents 53 & 54), and heard from the Drivers of Car 21 (Wharton) and Car 27 (David). On the approach to Turn 6, Car 27 was on the left (inside) and Car 21 on the right, with Car 21 attempting to pass around the outside of the corner. Car 27 stated that he was ahead of Car 21 at the apex of Turn 6 and was defending an outside overtake attempt. He stated that, in accordance with the F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines, Car 21 did not earn entitlement to the corner. Car 21 stated that he had the sufficient overlap (his front axle was ahead of Car 27’s front axle) to be entitled to racing room, and that the lack of room left by Car 27 forced him wide. He stated that he remained in full control of the car throughout the corner and was not aware that he had exceeded track limits due to the close proximity of the two cars. He added that, had he been aware he had left the track, he would have given the position back. Having considered the mater extensively, the Stewards were unable to definitely conclude, with sufficient clarity, the relative position of both cars at the apex of the corner. Accordingly, the Stewards decide to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 48 - DECISION - Car 27 - Allegedly forced Car 6 off track
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 27 - Allegedly forced Car 6 off track

details.fact: Car 27 (David) was alleged to have forced Car 6 (De Palo) off track at Turn 15.
details.infringement: Alleged Breach of Appendix L Chapter IV Article 2 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code
details.decision: No Further Action
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed the video evidence, summoned (Documents 45 & 46), and heard from the Drivers of Car 27 (David) and Car 6 (De Palo), together with their Team Representatives. On the approach to Turn 15, Car 27 was on the right (inside) and Car 6 on the left (outside), running side by side through the corner. The Driver of Car 27 stated that he was defending his position on the final lap of the race. Whilst aware that Car 6 was attempting to overtake, he maintained that Car 6 had not satisfied the criteria under the F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines for an outside overtake, and had therefore not earned the right to room at the exit of Turn 15. The Driver of Car 6 stated that, having gained a strong run under DRS, he drew alongside Car 27 and attempted to pass around the outside of Turn 15. He contended that Car 27 was carrying too much speed into the corner and had no proper means of defending his position at the exit. The F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines provide that, to be entitled to room (including at the exit) when overtaking on the outside of a corner, the overtaking car must: "have its front axle ahead of the front axle of the other car at the apex". The Stewards further note that overtaking on the outside of a high-speed corner carries an inherently greater level of risk, and the overtaking car must be ahead at the apex to establish entitlement to racing room. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was alongside, but not ahead of, Car 27 through the whole corner, and accordingly did not satisfy the criteria required to earn priority at the exit. As the obligation under the Guidelines to earn priority rests with the overtaking car, and Car 6 had not met that standard, the right to the corner remained with Car 27 as the defending car, and Car 6 was not forced off by Car 27. Accordingly, the Stewards decide to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 79 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 26 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 26 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 26 (Escotto) left the track at Turn 5 on Lap 1, rejoined and gained a lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. The video shows Car 26 (ESC) was behind Car 24 (MCL) at the apex for Turn 5 on Lap 1. ESC drove off the track, continued through the runoff area and rejoined after Turn 6 in front of MCL. Article 27.3 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations provides that once a car has gone off track it may re-join provided it does so “without gaining any lasting advantage”. Because ESC was defending, he would be expected to concede the position. Because he did not do so he retained a position to which he was not entitled. Failing to lose a position that should have fairly been lost constitutes gaining an advantage. The Stewards consider this to be an infringement and impose the baseline penalty which is consistent with penalties for breaches of a similar nature.

documents.title: Doc 70 - DECISION - Car 10 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage on Car 1
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 10 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage on Car 1

details.fact: Cars 1 (Nael) and 10 (Kato) were in close quarters at Turn 18 and Car 10 went off track and reentered in front of Car 1.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 67 & 68). The Stewards were requested to investigate the overall interaction of Car 1 (NAE) and Car 10 (KAT) at Turn 18. The investigation commenced from a neutral point of view meaning that neither party was alleged to be the primary offender. Instead, the Stewards examined related but separate questions: whether NAE forced KAT off track in between Turns 18 and 19 or whether KAT left the track at the exit of Turn 18 and gained a lasting advantage by doing so. Article 27.3 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations provides that once a car has gone off track it may re-join provided it does so “without gaining any lasting advantage”. Gaining a position constitutes gaining an advantage as does failing to lose a position that should have fairly been lost. In order to judge whether a position was gained or lost we must first determine the relative positions before and after. In this case the cars were in such close quarters at the apex of Turn 18 that it cannot be determined who was ahead at the point the cars should be judged. The Stewards, therefore, cannot make a clear determination whether KAT gained a position or merely retained one. If KAT was forced off while ahead, he is entitled to retain the position. To the contrary, if NAE had won the corner, he is not liable for forcing KAT off, and KAT would be obligated to lose the position. Since Document 69 was inconclusive as to whether or not NAE forced KAT off, it is impossible to determine here whether or not the circumstances required KAT to be behind NAE after re-joining to avoid retaining an unfair advantage. Based on the totality of these very narrow circumstances, the Stewards are not comfortably satisfied that KAT committed an infraction, and we therefore elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 69 - Decision - Car 1 - Allegedly forcing Car 10 off track
documents.subject: Decision - Car 1 - Allegedly forcing Car 10 off track

details.fact: Cars 1 (Nael) and 10 (Kato) were in close quarters at Turn 18 and Car 10 went off track and reentered in front of Car 1.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, 2b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 67 & 68). The stewards were requested to investigate the overall interaction of Car 1 (NAE) and Car 10 (KAT) at Turn 18. The investigation commenced from a neutral point of view meaning that neither party was alleged to be the primary offender. Instead, the Stewards examined separate but related questions: whether NAE forced KAT off track in between Turns 18 and 19 or whether KAT left the track at the exit of Turn 18 and gained a lasting advantage by doing so. Clearly NAE had his front axle at KAT’s mirror at the apex of T18. However, a driver attempting an inside overtake is expected to have his front axle to the mirror prior to and at the apex. Additional considerations are how the cars arrived to the apex (was the manoeuvre made too late or was it overly optimistic?). In this borderline case, the Stewards are not comfortably satisfied that NAE established his position early enough to have won the corner. Neither are we comfortably satisfied that he failed to do so. If he had won the corner he would not be guilty of forcing KAT off. Being unable to determine whether or not NAE had won the rights to the corner it cannot be fairly determined whether or not he is liable for forcing KAT off. Since the Stewards have not reached the threshold of being comfortably satisfied with their conclusion, we refrain from taking any further action.

documents.title: Doc 51 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 4 (Stromsted) collided with the rear of Car 27 (David) at Turn 13.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the 2026 International Sporting Code
details.decision: A 5-grid position penalty for both races at this Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 25 and 26). Car 4 (STR) collided with the rear of Car 27 (DAV) at Turn 13. DAV explained that he was experiencing congestion because the cars in front of him had been traveling slowly, then accelerating and aggressively braking for many corners. He stated that he was following Car 31 (XIE) out of Turn 13 while on the racing line, but that XIE did not accelerate as he expected. He then felt contact from behind and was taken out of the race. STR confirmed that the cars in front of him had been driving erratically since Turn 5. He attributed the collision to the erratic driving of the field, and not to any fault of his own. The Stewards note that a trailing car is generally held to be responsible for colliding with a car in front. The Stewards accept that the field was displaying multiple instances of erratic driving during the lap in question but determine that STR had every reason to expect it to continue. Under the circumstances, the Stewards conclude that it was not reasonable for STR to assume that cars would begin driving normally out of Turn 13 and that he had every reason to take extra caution in this situation. While the driving throughout the entire pack factored into the collision, the Stewards find STR to be predominantly at fault for running into the rear of DAV. The penalty imposed is in accordance with the penalty guidelines.

details.fact: Car 15 (Deligny) left the track at Turn 18.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations – a driver may not deliberately leave the track without a justifiable reason.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 15. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 20). Car 15 (EDE) overtook the car in front of it by leaving the track. The Stewards consider the act of driving off the track to conduct an overtaking manoeuvre in these circumstances is a precarious decision because it adds risk to an already crowded situation, especially when the inevitable rejoin occurs. The Stewards find the leaving of the track in these circumstances is not a justifiable reason and amounts to a breach of the Rules. The Stewards impose a Reprimand on the driver of Car 15 (EDE).

documents.title: Doc 33 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Practice start infringement in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Practice start infringement in Practice

details.fact: Car 17 (Clerot) did not follow the Race Director instructions - practice start performed with one car directly in front of him on the grid.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code and alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow Competition Notes, Item 15.2.b).
details.decision: Warning.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 18). The Driver of Car 17 (CLE) performed his practice start with a car directly in front of him on the grid. During the hearing, CLE explained that as soon as the car in front of him launched it went into anti-stall mode as it crept away from its grid position. CLE having already decided to perform his practice start, launched and had to pass to avoid. Competition Note 15.2.b) provides that “under no circumstances may a driver perform a practice start if another car in front of him is still stationary ahead on the same side of the grid.” Since the car in front was moving, it cannot be said that CLE violated that instruction, however the ISC provision against unsafe acts remains to be considered. In this case, the Stewards determine that CLE acted unsafely by performing his practice start before allowing the car in front to safely clear its grid position. Fortunately, this manoeuvre was not unsafe with respect to other cars. While CLE’s practice start did not expressly violate the Competition Notes, the Stewards determine that a warning is in order for failing to wait a reasonable amount of time before commencing his practice start.

Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 9 was in breach of Article 37.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations and impose a 10 second time penalty in accordance with the penalty guidelines.

documents.title: Doc 58 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 24 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 24 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 24 (MCL) left the track at Turn 1 on lap 1, overtaking Car 30 off track and retaining the position.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. At the start of the race, on Lap 1 at Turn 1, Car 24 left the track while overtaking Car 30. Car 24 completed the overtake off the track and retained the position after rejoining. Under Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations, a driver may rejoin the track only when it is safe to do so and without gaining any lasting advantage. The Stewards determined that Car 24 gained a lasting advantage by overtaking Car 30 off the track and keeping the position. However, taking into account the Lap 1, Turn 1 circumstances, the Stewards considered these to be mitigating factors and therefore imposed the above five-second time penalty, with no driver penalty points.

documents.title: Doc 57 - DECISION - Car 28 - Collision involving Car 23 and Car 28 in Race 2
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 28 - Collision involving Car 23 and Car 28 in Race 2

details.fact: Car 23 (Shin) and Car 28 (Barrichello) had a collision at Turn 4.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 23 (SHI) was attempting an outside pass on Car 28 (BAR) at Turn 4. SHI was trailing slightly at the apex and had not earned the rights to the corner. The cars maintained overlap with BAR pulling ahead from the apex to the exit. A collision occurred as they tracked out to the exit curb. Typically, such a collision would be charged to the car on the outside that had not established its rights, however the Stewards note that BAR on the inside tracked out earlier than normal for the corner which played into the collision with BAR who could not simply disappear. Under the circumstances the Stewards determine that neither driver was wholly or predominantly at fault for the collision. Accordingly, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 50 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 12 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 12 - Technical infringement

details.fact: Car 12 (Le) was found to be 3kg below the required minimum weight of 729kg.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 4.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Disqualification of Car 12 from the Classification of Race 1. All cars originally classified behind Car 12 are moved up one place in the Race classification.
details.reason: The Stewards received a report from the Technical Delegate (Document 47). They summoned and heard the Driver and Team Representative (Document 48). The Technical Delegate reported that Car 12 (KLE) was weighed after Race 1 and was found to be 726kg, which is 3.0kg below the minimum weight of 729kg - as stipulated in Article 4.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations. The Team Representative explained that they have conducted a preliminary investigation into the cause of being below the minimum weight and found that Car 12’s water pressure dropped significantly after the car got hit by some gravel due to another car going off track. The team argued that the loss of liquid from the car’s cooling system was the cause of being below the minimum weight. The Stewards thanked the Team Representative for bringing forward this explanation and justification. Unfortunately the team had no way of proving the weight of the fluid lost or that the car was compliant before the loss. The Stewards reminded the Team Representative of the International Court of Appeal’s (ICA) long-standing and consistent jurisprudence that the obligation to comply with the technical regulations and the liability incurred as a result of noncompliance lie solely with competitors. Furthermore, the Stewards also explained that the long-standing sanction and ICA jurisprudence for a technical compliance has been a sanction of disqualification. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine this is breach of Article 4.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations and accordingly decided to disqualify Car 12 from the F3 Sprint race results.

documents.title: Doc 39 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 30 - Weaving on straight
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 30 - Weaving on straight

details.fact: Car 30 (BHI) moved 6 times from Turn 3 to Turn 4 when defending its position.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 b) of the International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 penalty points to be added to driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 penalty points
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (Documents 37 and 38). Car 27 attempted to overtake Car 30 between Turn 3 and Turn 4. While defending, Car 30 changed direction six times on the straight. The Stewards determined that these repeated changes of direction were erratic and went beyond what is permitted when defending a position. Car 30 also failed to leave sufficient racing room for Car 27 when returning to the racing line at Turn 4. Accordingly, the Stewards imposed the penalty which is within the standard range under the guidelines.

documents.title: Doc 29 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 30 - Stopping in fast lane
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 30 - Stopping in fast lane

details.fact: Car 30 (BHI) stopped in the fast lane.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the International Sporting Code (failure to comply with the Race Director’s Competition Notes – 16.3)
details.decision: A fine of €2,000 is imposed on the Team. Of this amount, €1,000 shall be paid in accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code. The fine must be paid within forty-eight hours of notification by bank transfer to the FIA. The remaining €1,000 is suspended for the remainder of the 2026 Formula 3 season in accordance with Article 12.4.6 of the FIA International Sporting Code, subject to there being no further breach by the Team of Competition Note 16.3 or any successor thereto relating to stopping in or blocking the fast lane.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and summoned and heard the driver and team representative (Document 22). Car 30 entered the pit lane, approached its garage, and was stopped by a team mechanic in the fast lane. The team then pushed the car back, which blocked the fast lane and delayed five cars behind it. The representative accepted that the team made an error by positioning the mechanic in the fast lane and instructing Car 30 to stop there. The Driver of Car 30 stated that he followed the mechanic’s instructions and believed he had stopped in the correct position to be pushed back. Having considered the matter, the Stewards determined that the team was at fault for stopping Car 30 in the fast lane and causing the obstruction. Therefore, a proportionate fine is imposed on the team.

documents.title: Doc 28 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - Impeding of Car 19 in Qualifying
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - Impeding of Car 19 in Qualifying

details.fact: Car 9 (Giusti) impeded car 19 (Ho) at Turn 3
details.infringement: Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 b) of the FIA International Sporting Code and Article 31.6 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint and Feature Races at this Competition. There are no penalty points associated with this decision.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video and GPS telemetry evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (Documents 23 & 24). With time winding down in the qualifying session, Car 9 (GIU) commenced a push lap, exceeded track limits at Turn 1, and rejoined in front of CHO with 10 seconds remaining on the session clock. CHO, who had a clean run through turn 1, was closing on GIU after his re-entry. At this point GIU’s session was effectively over since time was up and his lap was destined to be deleted. GIU explained that he continued at full pace hoping to get another push lap in. Unfortunately, GIU’s team had not informed him that the session was over. CHO caught GIU at T3. GIU slowed significantly more than CHO at Turn 3 before ultimately letting him pass on the exit. The stewards agree with GIU that just because he went off track that he was not obligated to adopt a cool down or prep strategy for the remainder of the lap. GIU stated that he was pushing and that as such he was not liable for impeding. GIU had the right to continue to push, however his telemetry at Turn 3 with CHO directly behind was not consistent with a car that was continuing to push. Under the circumstances, the Stewards determine that GIU unnecessarily impeded CHO at T3. The penalty imposed is specified by the penalty guidelines and is consistent with past precedents for similar infractions.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Impeding of Car 17 in Practice

details.fact: Car 17 (Clerot) was impeded by Cars 1 (Nael) and 23 (Shin) who were driving slowly and side-by-side at Turn 6.

details.decision: Warning given to the Driver of Car 23.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 14, 15 and 16). Car 1 (NAE) and Car 23 (SHI) were driving slowly and side-by-side from Turn 4 to Turn 6. Car 17 (CLE) was on a push lap and locked his brakes in avoidance of NAE and SHI at Turn 6. Article 19 of the Competition Notes makes it clear that, “At no time during Practice/Qualifying should drivers remain side by side. When drivers are on the racing line, they must ensure that they are travelling at a speed sufficient not to unnecessarily impede any driver on or starting a fast lap.” In this case, SHI was driving slowly on the racing line and SHI and NAE were driving side by side. The Stewards determine that SHI and NAE unnecessarily impeded CLE. The penalty issued is in accordance with the penalty guidelines and past precedents for such an infraction during the Practice session.

documents.title: Doc 13 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 30 - Failure to follow RD instructions
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 30 - Failure to follow RD instructions

details.fact: Car 30 (Bhirombhakdi) did not follow the Race Director Competition Notes - practice start performed with car 25 stationary ahead of him on the grid.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 30. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 11). The Driver of Car 30 (BHI) stopped behind car 25 (NAK) to perform his practice start on the right grid lane. Art. 16.2 b) of the F3 Spielberg Competition Notes (document 3) states that ”Under no circumstances should a driver make a practice start if another car is still stationary ahead on the same side of the grid”. During the hearing the driver stated that he had planned to do the staring procedure on the left side of the grid, but saw it was too crowded so he switched to the right lane. He saw that car 25 was in front of him but he thought that he had already completed his practice starting procedure. Driver of car 30 acknowledges that he should have been more attentive in the situation and understand the possible repercussions of his actions. This is a possible safety issue, however the Stewards determine that the present situation did not rise to the level of danger. Accordingly, the Stewards issue a Driving Reprimand.

documents.title: Doc 12 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 1 - Took chequered flag twice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 1 - Took chequered flag twice

details.fact: Car 1 (NAEL) took the chequered flag twice.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 31.9 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 1. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and GPS track map evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (Document 10). The chequered flag was out and displayed less than two seconds before car 1 reached the line. Upon seeing the video replay the driver acknowledged that he noticed the red lights at the gantry also had an opportunity to see the flag, but he was distracted following the car in front at the moment. While flag violations often incur significant penalties, there was no inherent safety issue in this case. Accordingly, the stewards issue a driving reprimand.
